topStories.headline: Port Hosts Community Open House on Fisherman's Wharf Forward Long-Term Plan
topStories.dek: Residents and waterfront stakeholders gathered Wednesday at Pier 45 to weigh in on concept designs for the Taylor Street shoreline and Inner Lagoon.
topStories.body:
The Port of San Francisco held a community open house on Wednesday, September 9, inviting the public to review and comment on concept design options for the longer-term phase of its Fisherman's Wharf Forward initiative. Attendees had the opportunity to learn about and provide feedback on design options and strategies being considered for the Taylor Street shoreline and Inner Lagoon, with light food and child-friendly activities provided. The event ran from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m. at the USS Pampanito Triangle Space at Pier 45 Shed A.

The longer-term work — distinct from the near-term plaza and lagoon improvements already underway — is ambitious in scope. According to the Port's project page, longer-term efforts will focus on resilience infrastructure designed to adapt Taylor Street and the Inner Lagoon through 2100, including strengthening or replacing the seawall and wharves, flood-proofing buildings, improving facilities for the fishing fleet and fishing industry, developing and leasing retail spaces, and enhancements to the public realm.

Public outreach and engagement throughout 2026 will inform these longer-term efforts, with a goal of having a conceptual plan completed by early 2027. A prior public meeting on April 30 was described in the Fisherman's Wharf Advisory Committee's May 6 minutes as well attended both in person and online. Construction of the plaza at the former Alioto's restaurant site has remained on track; the team has made progress preparing the café space of the Grotto building for a future tenant, and both the plaza and the tenanted café space were anticipated to open in summer 2026.

Stakeholders wishing to follow the project can sign up for notifications through the Fisherman's Wharf Advisory Committee at sfport.com/fwforward.

topStories.headline: Club Fugazi Launches Its First Comedy Festival, Running Through Saturday Night
topStories.dek: The North Beach theater is hosting the inaugural Fugazi Funny Festival this week — four nights of stand-up, storytelling, and musical comedy at 678 Green Street.
topStories.body:
Club Fugazi launched the inaugural Fugazi Funny Festival, a four-night celebration of comedy featuring acclaimed comedians, storytellers, and musical comedy taking place at North Beach's iconic entertainment venue from September 9 through 12, 2026. The festival brings together an eclectic lineup of performers for an intimate series of evenings designed to showcase the many forms comedy can take.

The lineup runs as follows: Wednesday's opener was 'Besties: A Friendly Comedy & Music Show,' hosted by comedian Xander Beltran and musician Spencer James, blending stand-up sets, original and cover live music from the Besties House Band, and on-the-fly improvised musical comedy. Thursday featured Story Night with Diane Amos, a nationally recognized actress, comedian, and professional storyteller based in San Francisco. Friday brings cult-favorite Eddie Pepitone, known for appearances on Conan, Chappelle's Show, and It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia. Saturday closes the festival with Shane Mauss, a stand-up comedian who synthesizes comedy, evolutionary biology, and psychedelic exploration.

Tickets for remaining performances are on sale at clubfugazisf.com, with pre-sale prices of $38.50 and walk-up prices at $44. A festival pass covering all four nights was also available for $90. All events feature general admission seating, run approximately 90 minutes, and include a two-drink minimum. Doors open 45 minutes before each show.

Club Fugazi is best known as the home of the Dear San Francisco acrobatic show by The 7 Fingers, which resumes its regular run after the festival closes Saturday. The comedy festival is the venue's first dedicated comedy programming series since the show opened in September 2021.

topStories.headline: Burned-Out Verdi Building Cleared for Partial Demolition — Site Now Listed for Sale
topStories.dek: After the Board of Appeals unanimously rejected a resident's appeal in May, the fire-damaged Coit Liquors corner at 659 Union Street and an adjacent garage have been placed on the market as an unentitled development parcel.
topStories.body:
The Verdi Building at 659 Union Street — known to many North Beach residents as the former Coit Liquors building — has entered a new chapter after years of stalled redevelopment. The city's Board of Appeals unanimously rejected an appeal that had halted the emergency partial demolition of the structure on May 20, clearing developer Red Bridge Partners to resume work. According to a June 24, 2026 report by SocketSite, the partially demolished Verdi Building and adjacent parking garage at 1636 Powell Street have since been placed on the market as a combined, un-entitled 18,000-square-foot development site described as being at the epicenter of San Francisco's historic North Beach neighborhood, with flexible zoning permitting a wide variety of uses including residential.

The building has been empty since fires gutted it in 2013 and again in 2018, displacing 32 rent-controlled tenants in the first blaze and a liquor store in the second. Parts of the facade have been held up by metal bracing and prompted sidewalk closures and a bus stop relocation. The city's Board of Appeals cleared work to resume on removing approximately 50 feet of unstable brick wall at the rear of the building. Supervisor Danny Sauter praised the board's decision, saying commissioners appropriately prioritized public safety despite concerns from historic preservation advocates who worry the ruling could pave the way for the building's eventual full demolition.

The Telegraph Hill Dwellers, on behalf of its more than 500 members, had urged the Board of Appeals to condition any demolition permit on tenants' right to return and adherence to the developer's 2023 plans, which had enjoyed widespread community support. Those conditions were not imposed. Original plans by Red Bridge Partners for 23 rental units with a rooftop restaurant were abandoned, with developer Jeff Jurow citing rising construction costs. No buyer or new development application has been publicly announced.

events.title: Fugazi Funny Festival — Eddie Pepitone (Fri.) & Shane Mauss (Sat.)
events.location: Club Fugazi, 678 Green Street, North Beach
events.description: The inaugural Fugazi Funny Festival closes with cult-favorite stand-up Eddie Pepitone on Friday and science-meets-comedy storyteller Shane Mauss on Saturday. Tickets $38.50 pre-sale / $44 walk-up at clubfugazisf.com; two-drink minimum, general admission.

events.title: Fish Market at the Wharf
events.description: Local fishers sell directly to the public every Saturday through September at this pop-up market operated by the fishing community in partnership with the Fisherman's Wharf Community Benefit District and the Port of San Francisco. Fresh and flash-frozen catches rotate weekly.

events.title: Pier Party at the Wharf — Free Live Music
events.description: The Fisherman's Wharf Community Benefit District's free outdoor concert series returns for its second-Saturday edition, with live music, a craft cocktail bar, bistro seating, and waterfront views. Free and open to all; follow @pierpartysf on Instagram for performer updates.

events.title: Dear San Francisco — Ongoing at Club Fugazi
events.location: Club Fugazi, 678 Green Street, North Beach
events.description: The 7 Fingers' acclaimed immersive acrobatic circus show celebrating San Francisco's history runs year-round at the neighborhood's historic theater. Performances Wednesday–Sunday; tickets from $49 to $89 at clubfugazisf.com.

events.title: Pier Party at Sunset — Final Edition of 2026
events.location: Taylor Street Triangle Lot, Fisherman's Wharf
events.description: The last fourth-Saturday sunset session of the 2026 Pier Party series brings live music, dancing, and golden-hour Bay views to the waterfront. Free and open to the public; follow @pierpartysf on Instagram for lineup updates.

moreNews.headline: Port Conducting Pier 47 Substructure Repairs at Fisherman's Wharf This Summer
moreNews.body: The Port of San Francisco is carrying out structural repairs on the western portion of Pier 47's substructure during summer 2026, according to Fisherman's Wharf Advisory Committee meeting minutes from May 6, 2026. Condition assessments conducted in 2025 identified elements needing stabilization to allow existing operations to continue. Pier 47 serves both visitors and commercial fishing vessels at the heart of the waterfront.
moreNews.sourceName: Port of San Francisco — FWAC Meeting Minutes, May 6, 2026

restaurants.name: Original Joe's
restaurants.description: An SF institution for over 80 years, celebrated for its signature red leather booths, veal Marsala, house-made ravioli, and classic cocktails.

restaurants.name: North Beach Restaurant
restaurants.description: A North Beach anchor for over five decades, serving handmade pasta, home-cured prosciutto, Chicken Mattone, and an extensive Italian wine list.

restaurants.name: Tosca Cafe
restaurants.description: Open since 1919, this legendary Columbus Avenue bar is famous for its house cappuccino cocktail (armagnac, bourbon, and steamed milk), meatballs, and dimly lit late-night vibe.

restaurants.name: Vesuvio Cafe
restaurants.description: Founded in 1948 and frequented by Jack Kerouac, Allen Ginsberg, and the Beat Generation, this iconic saloon across from City Lights remains a North Beach anchor for poets, artists, and bon vivants.

restaurants.name: Caffe Trieste
restaurants.description: San Francisco's oldest espresso bar, open since 1956 and beloved for its dark roast coffee, opera on the jukebox, and storied Beat Generation atmosphere.

restaurants.name: Butter & Crumble
restaurants.description: North Beach's most-queued-for bakery, known for inventive laminated pastries including a pistachio-cardamom croissant and a mortadella-Gruyère 'morty p,' selling out daily by mid-morning.

restaurants.name: Liguria Bakery
restaurants.description: A North Beach institution since 1911, Liguria sells only focaccia — baked fresh each morning in a handful of classic flavors — and closes when it sells out.

restaurants.name: Bodega SF
restaurants.type: Natural wine bar and small plates
restaurants.description: A lively Columbus Avenue natural wine bar with a pink-neon glow and a hi-fi sound system, pouring Argentine, Spanish, Portuguese, and Turkish bottles alongside globally inflected small plates.

restaurants.name: Fanoos Grills
restaurants.description: Fast-casual counter serving halal shawarma, falafel, and kebabs as bowls or wraps; the second SF location of this popular concept, opened in 2026 with city grant support.

restaurants.name: Equal Parts SF
restaurants.description: A lively California-cuisine destination at the historic Old Spaghetti Factory space, featuring shareable seafood, braised meats, roasted whole fish, and creative cocktails in a plant-filled interior.

restaurants.name: Caffe Sport
restaurants.description: A flamboyantly decorated North Beach institution serving robust Sicilian-inflected seafood pastas, garlic prawns, and a boisterous atmosphere that has drawn loyal regulars for decades.

restaurants.name: Delancey Street Restaurant
restaurants.description: Part of the Delancey Street Foundation, this waterfront restaurant at the Embarcadero serves hearty American fare and is staffed entirely by residents of the nonprofit's rehabilitation program.

restaurants.name: Fog Harbor Fish House
restaurants.description: A pier-side Fisherman's Wharf classic serving sustainably sourced Dungeness crab, cioppino, sourdough clam chowder, and bay views from Pier 39.

restaurants.name: Boudin Bakery & Café
restaurants.description: Home of San Francisco's original sourdough since 1849, with a flagship Fisherman's Wharf location featuring a museum, bakery theater, and café serving classic clam chowder bread bowls.

restaurants.name: In-N-Out Burger
restaurants.description: The only In-N-Out location in San Francisco, perched at the edge of Fisherman's Wharf with outdoor bay views and perpetual lines for its Double-Double.

restaurants.name: Scoma's Restaurant
restaurants.description: A Fisherman's Wharf landmark since 1965, Scoma's is celebrated for fresh Dungeness crab, sand dabs, and cioppino served steps from the working fishing fleet on Pier 47.

restaurants.name: Café Greco
restaurants.description: A beloved Columbus Avenue neighborhood café known for its superb espresso, welcoming sidewalk seating, and old-world Italian café atmosphere at the heart of North Beach.

restaurants.name: Sotto Mare
restaurants.description: A packed, beloved North Beach trattoria legendary for its cioppino — a heaping pot of fresh local seafood — along with whole Dungeness crab and homemade pasta.

restaurants.name: Julius' Castle
restaurants.description: The 1924 Telegraph Hill landmark below Coit Tower, reopening after nearly two decades closed following a restoration of its fire-damaged turret and original wood panelling.

hotels.name: Argonaut Hotel
hotels.description: A nautically themed luxury boutique hotel housed in the historic 1907 Haslett Warehouse at Fisherman's Wharf, with exposed brick, Douglas Fir beams, and views of the Bay, Alcatraz, and the Golden Gate Bridge.

hotels.name: Hyatt Centric Fisherman's Wharf
hotels.description: A well-located full-service hotel steps from Pier 39, offering a sun deck, 24-hour fitness center, and convenient access to the Wharf's restaurants and attractions.

hotels.name: San Francisco Marriott Fisherman's Wharf
hotels.description: A large Marriott property steps from the Wharf offering the Red Fin Restaurant & Lounge, flexible meeting space, and easy walking access to Pier 39, Ghirardelli Square, and Aquatic Park.

hotels.name: Courtyard by Marriott San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf
hotels.description: A modern hotel steps from Pier 39 and the North Beach neighborhood, featuring Table580 restaurant, comfortable guest rooms, and valet parking.

hotels.name: Hotel Zoe Fisherman's Wharf
hotels.description: A contemporary boutique hotel in the heart of Fisherman's Wharf offering stylishly appointed rooms, in-room spa services, and walkable access to the bay waterfront.

hotels.name: Hotel Riu Plaza Fisherman's Wharf
hotels.description: A 4-star hotel at the edge of Fisherman's Wharf offering modern rooms, rooftop views, and a central position between North Beach and the waterfront.

hotels.name: San Remo Hotel
hotels.description: A charming Italianate Victorian hotel dating from 1906, offering budget-friendly shared-bath rooms in a beautifully preserved building near the boundary of North Beach and Fisherman's Wharf.

hotels.name: Hotel Caza Fisherman's Wharf
hotels.description: A boutique hotel near the waterfront offering comfortable, design-forward rooms with proximity to Pier 39, Ghirardelli Square, and the North Beach dining scene.

hotels.name: Fairmont Heritage Place, Ghirardelli Square
hotels.description: Upscale residence-style suites set within the landmarked Ghirardelli Square complex, offering full kitchens, multiple rooms, and sweeping views of the Bay and Golden Gate Bridge.

hotels.name: Hotel Zephyr San Francisco
hotels.description: A playful nautical-themed lifestyle hotel at Fisherman's Wharf featuring an outdoor game courtyard, fire pits, and a lobby bar with a community-focused atmosphere.

shops.name: City Lights Booksellers & Publishers
shops.description: The legendary North Beach bookstore and publisher founded by Lawrence Ferlinghetti in 1953 — the nation's first all-paperback bookstore — remains a global landmark for poetry, politics, and literary fiction, open daily 10 AM–10 PM.

shops.name: Grocery Outlet
shops.description: The neighborhood's long-awaited full-service grocery store, opened August 13 at the former Safeway site, independently operated by Jacqueline and Joel Lanoie with deeply discounted branded groceries.

shops.name: Ghirardelli Square
shops.description: The iconic landmarked chocolate factory converted into a retail and dining complex, anchored by the original Ghirardelli Chocolate Manufactory and sundae shop, with bay views and boutique shops.

shops.name: The Winery SF
shops.description: An urban winery in the Fisherman's Wharf area offering tastings of house-made California wines produced on-site, available for walk-in and by appointment.

shops.name: North Face Store
shops.description: The North Face's original flagship store — the brand was founded in San Francisco — carrying the full line of outdoor apparel, footwear, and gear at the edge of North Beach.

shops.name: Pier 39 Shops
shops.description: Over 90 shops and boutiques on the two-level pier attraction, ranging from locally themed gifts and jewelry to apparel and toys, with bay views and the famous sea lion colony at K-Dock.

shops.name: Levi's Plaza Farmers Market
shops.description: A weekly farmers market at Levi Strauss's waterfront corporate plaza, offering fresh produce, prepared foods, and artisan goods from local Bay Area vendors.

shops.name: AB Fits
shops.type: Independent denim and contemporary clothing boutique
shops.description: A well-curated North Beach boutique specializing in premium denim and contemporary clothing for men and women, with knowledgeable staff and a loyal neighborhood following.

shops.name: Aria
shops.type: Vintage and antique home goods shop
shops.description: A treasured North Beach shop dealing in European vintage jewelry, antique textiles, and decorative objects, beloved by designers and collectors for its carefully selected inventory.

shops.name: Schein & Schein
shops.description: A North Beach institution dealing in rare antique maps, charts, and prints — a singular resource for collectors and history enthusiasts on Grant Avenue.

artEntertainment.name: Club Fugazi
artEntertainment.description: A North Beach landmark since 1913, now home to the long-running immersive circus show 'Dear San Francisco' and upcoming Fugazi Funny Festival comedy series; seats approximately 300.

artEntertainment.name: Coit Tower
artEntertainment.description: The 1933 art deco column atop Telegraph Hill features Depression-era WPA murals inside and a 360-degree observation deck with sweeping views of the Bay, Golden Gate Bridge, and Alcatraz; open 10 AM–6 PM daily through October.

artEntertainment.name: USS Pampanito
artEntertainment.description: A meticulously restored World War II fleet submarine and National Historic Landmark at Pier 45, open daily 10 AM–6 PM for self-guided audio tours and group programs.

artEntertainment.name: San Francisco Maritime National Historical Park Visitor Center
artEntertainment.type: National Park visitor center and museum
artEntertainment.description: Free admission visitor center at the west end of Fisherman's Wharf with exhibits on Pacific Coast maritime history; note that Hyde Street Pier and its historic ships are currently closed for the Hyde Street Rebuild Project.

artEntertainment.name: San Francisco Maritime Museum
artEntertainment.description: A striking 1939 Streamline Moderne building at Aquatic Park (900 Beach St) housing ship models, WPA-era murals of sealife, and exhibits on maritime history; free admission, open Wednesday–Sunday.

artEntertainment.name: Pier 39 Sea Lion Viewing Area
artEntertainment.description: The famous K-Dock colony of California sea lions — which took up residence in 1990 — can be viewed year-round for free from the west marina of Pier 39, with interpretive signage provided by the Marine Mammal Center.

artEntertainment.name: Cobb's Comedy Club
artEntertainment.description: San Francisco's largest comedy club in the heart of North Beach, hosting nationally touring headliners and local showcases with a two-drink minimum; shows are 18+ with valid ID.

artEntertainment.name: SkyStar Observation Wheel
artEntertainment.description: A 150-foot observation wheel at Fisherman's Wharf offering gondola rides with panoramic views of the Bay, Golden Gate Bridge, and Alcatraz from the waterfront.

gymsRecreation.name: Yoga 906
gymsRecreation.type: Yoga studio in a historic church
gymsRecreation.description: A striking yoga studio housed in a 117-year-old deconsecrated church at 906 Broadway, offering classes for all levels in a soaring, architecturally stunning space on the North Beach/Russian Hill border.

gymsRecreation.name: Orangetheory Fitness North Beach
gymsRecreation.type: Heart rate zone interval training studio
gymsRecreation.description: A high-energy group fitness studio on Columbus Avenue offering 60-minute heart-rate-monitored workouts combining treadmill cardio and strength training with triple-certified coaches.

gymsRecreation.name: F45 Training North Beach
gymsRecreation.description: A high-intensity 45-minute circuit training studio at 350 Bay Street, offering daily varied workouts in strength, cardio, and hybrid formats with a strong community atmosphere.

gymsRecreation.name: Bay Club San Francisco
gymsRecreation.description: A premium full-service sports club serving the North Beach and Telegraph Hill area, offering a gym floor, group fitness classes, basketball, tennis, squash courts, and a pool.

gymsRecreation.name: Aquatic Park / San Francisco Bay Swimming
gymsRecreation.description: The protected cove at the foot of Fisherman's Wharf, beloved by open-water swimmers and the South End Rowing Club, with a sandy beach and views of the Golden Gate Bridge; free and open year-round.

gymsRecreation.name: Washington Square Park
gymsRecreation.description: North Beach's beloved green heart — a tree-lined square where early-morning tai chi practitioners, dog walkers, and picnickers share space under the shadow of Saints Peter and Paul Church.

gymsRecreation.name: Levi's Plaza Park
gymsRecreation.description: A handsome landscaped park at the foot of Telegraph Hill designed by Lawrence Halprin, with granite fountains, lawns, and a stream channel — a quiet midday retreat popular with workers and walkers.

gymsRecreation.name: Filbert Steps and Telegraph Hill Trails
gymsRecreation.description: The famous wooden staircases and garden paths ascending the east face of Telegraph Hill, home to the wild cherry-headed conures (parrots), lush cottage gardens, and breathtaking Bay views.

gymsRecreation.name: Chinatown YMCA
gymsRecreation.description: A full-service community YMCA serving the neighborhoods bordering North Beach and Chinatown, offering gym equipment, fitness classes, and a pool.
